seo.description: Grounds maintenance, landscape projects, irrigation and tree care for View Royal homes and stratas, with tree bylaw checks before work. Get a free quote.

intro: View Royal includes waterfront homes on Portage Inlet, family homes in Helmcken and Atkins, townhouse stratas and healthcare and institutional grounds.

View Royal's bylaw protects species including shore pine and trees with raptor, osprey or heron nests. Most removals or alterations need a permit. See [irrigation](/services/irrigation/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/).
See [sample projects](/projects/) and our [seasonal guides](/resources/) for more.

localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

View Royal's Tree Protection Bylaw No. 1069 (2022) protects species including shore pine, replacement trees, trees with raptor, osprey or heron nests, trees kept as a permit condition and Town trees. Removing or altering protected trees generally needs a Tree Removal or Alteration Permit; pruning branches up to 10 cm by an ISA certified arborist is exempt, and emergency removals need notice with photos by the next business day.

The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.
